(a) **Chiral and Achiral Molecules**:
- **Chiral Molecule**: A molecule that is not superimposable on its mirror image. It lacks a plane or center of symmetry and exhibits optical activity (e.g., Lactic acid).
- **Achiral Molecule**: A molecule that is superimposable on its mirror image. It possesses at least one element of symmetry (e.g., Propanoic acid).

| Feature | Chiral Molecules | Achiral Molecules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mirror image | Non-superimposable | Superimposable |
| Optical activity | Optically active | Optically inactive |
| Symmetry | Asymmetric / Dissymmetric | Possesses plane/center of symmetry |

(b) **Enantiomers**: 
Enantiomers are stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other. 
*Example*: D-glyceraldehyde and L-glyceraldehyde.
- **Physical Properties**: Enantiomers share identical physical properties (melting point, boiling point, density, refractive index) except for the direction in which they rotate plane-polarized light.
- **Chemical Properties**: They possess identical chemical reactivities towards achiral reagents, but react differently with chiral reagents and exhibit different biological activities.

(c) **Optical Activity**: 
The ability of a chiral substance to rotate the plane of polarization of plane-polarized light when it passes through a solution of the substance.

```text
[Light Source] ---> [Polarizer] ---> [Sample Tube (Polarimeter)] ---> [Analyzer] ---> [Observer]
 (Unpolarized)    (Plane-Polarized)     (Contains Chiral Solution)      (Rotated Light) 
```
proTip: Always highlight that enantiomers differ only in their optical rotation direction and chiral-specific biological/chemical interactions.
